name: Ashveil Tunnel Runner's Compressed Rig
description: Designed — if that word applies to something assembled from desperation and ingenuity — for moving fast through the Shelf's sub-infrastructure tunnels. The core piece is a long-sleeved base layer in matte charcoal, cut close to the body and treated with a rubberized coating along the forearms and shoulders for sliding through tight passages without tearing. Over it sits a sleeveless tactical vest, originally a Vantablack surplus piece with the branding sliced off and replaced with hand-stitched patches of various gray and black fabrics. Sixteen pockets of various sizes distribute weight evenly across the torso — some sealed with original magnetic closures still functioning, others sewn shut with fishing line, others left open for fast access. Trousers are skintight reinforced leggings in dark charcoal with articulated knee panels cut from a yoga mat and stitched in — ugly but effective padding. Over the thighs, a pair of salvaged thigh pockets are strapped directly to the legs with nylon webbing. The shoes are flat-soled, thin, and hand-repaired: originally a Patchwork Runner Low, now barely recognizable under layers of rubber adhesive patches and re-lacing with paracord. The face is partially covered by a wrap of dark gray filter cloth — not a proper respirator, but better than breathing raw tunnel air. A salvaged chrome forearm plate from a junked augmentation rig is strapped to the left forearm as a makeshift shield and tool surface, its exposed circuit traces long dead but the alloy still hard.
materials: assorted gray and black patch fabrics
functionality: Rubberized forearms and shoulders reduce tunnel abrasion. Sixteen-pocket distribution system for survival gear. Articulated knee padding for crawling and crouching. Flat thin soles for maximum tactile feedback on unstable surfaces. Filter cloth reduces particulate inhalation. Salvaged chrome forearm plate provides impact and slash protection on left arm. Full range of motion prioritized throughout.
what_it_says: Speed and access. This person needs to move through spaces most people can't enter and can't afford to be slowed down by gear. The stripped Vantablack vest with the branding cut off is a quiet statement — someone who knows the value of what they're wearing and refuses to advertise someone else's name on their body.
worn_by: people who need to disappear fast
story_hooks: The salvaged chrome forearm plate, when examined by someone with technical knowledge, turns out to be from a military-grade augmentation rig — the kind that isn't supposed to exist below Tier 4. How did it end up strapped to a Shelf runner's arm with nylon webbing?

A Vantablack Internal Security analyst spots the silhouette of their company's vest construction under all the modifications — even with the branding cut off, the pocket arrangement is a proprietary pattern, and the wearer is now a person of interest in an equipment theft investigation.
In a collapsed tunnel section, the filter cloth wrap and rubberized forearms are the only things keeping the wearer alive while they wait for rescue — or decide not to wait.
